newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada January housing starts rise 7.8 pct. [CORRECTED 13:57 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Canada January housing starts rise 7.8 pct. [CORRECTED 13:57 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects to remove para forecasting housing starts.)

Canadian housing starts rose by 7.8 percent in January to a seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR) of 145,000 units from a revised 134,500 units in December, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp (CMHC) said on Monday.
Actual housing starts fell to 7,247 in January from a revised 10,163 the month before. The SAAR is a monthly figure adjusted to remove normal seasonal variations and multiplied by 12.

The housing corporation said that although longer-term mortgage rates edged up in January, the active resale market and declining inventories of newly completed and unocupied houses pushed new home building in several provinces.
"The January figures are the best since November 1994," said Michel Laurence, senior economist at the CMHC market analysis center.
